glosses: bad, useless, of poor quality; lousy, rubbish

examples.text: Фиго́вый из тебя́ пло́тник.

glosses: связанный, соотносящийся по значению с существительным фига

examples.text: Фиговый листок.
В дорогу взяли самый фиговый бензин, какой только смогли найти, дабы в зажравшейся буржуйляндии можно было бодяжить их хороший бензин с нашим.
No offense, but his cooking is lousy.
I cleaned the lousy garage.
I caught a cold and I've been feeling lousy all week.
I've had enough of lousy backstabbing at this place.

glosses: Filled or packed (with something, usually bad).

examples.text: The place was lousy with students.

The benignant influence crept like gas through the Row. […] And triangulation might possibly have located it in the Palace Flophouse and Grill. Certainly the Palace was lousy with it. Mack and the boys were charged. Jones was seen to leap from his chair only to do a quick tap dance and sit down again.
[I talked to] Annabeth about the Greek gods who hung out in New York and made her life difficult. Apparently North America was lousy with ancient gods. We had a full-blown infestation.

glosses: Of perishable items, overridden with bacteria and other infectious agents.

examples.text: If you leave a bin unattended for a few weeks, the rubbish inside will turn rotten.

Antonio: Mark you this, Bassanio, / The devil can cite Scripture for his purpose. / An evil soul producing holy witness / Is like a villain with a smiling cheek, / A goodly apple rotten at the heart. / O, what a goodly outside falsehood hath!
The floors were damaged and the walls were rotten.
His mouth stank and his teeth were rotten.
But poore old man, thou prun'ſt a rotten tree, / That cannot ſo much as a bloſſome yeelde
That man is a rotten father.
This rotten policy will create more injustice in this country.
Something is rotten in the State of Denmarke.
Why is the weather always rotten in this city?
It was a rotten idea to take the boat out today.
She has the flu and feels rotten.

glosses: Of stone or rock, crumbling or friable; in a loose or disintegrated state.

examples.text: The quartz specimens were sometimes blue, hard-looking stone, or rotten quartz largely impregnated with iron, in both cases carrying bright glittering nodules of gold.
That kid is spoilt rotten.
The girls fancy him something rotten.
"It's old man Challenger's show and we are here by his good will, so it would be rotten bad form if we didn't follow his instructions to the letter."
"You're not only crazy," Oscar said bitterly, "you're rotten jealous. You can go to hell." He stomped away.
